1: [Ginza Rabba, Right I — The first life]

In the name of the Great Life, the sublime light, the supreme light that is above all works. The Life began to fashion the worlds, and the worlds were not worthy; and the Life rested, and the Life is patient, for the Life is without beginning and without end, and His patience is the length of His days.

There was a wellspring in the height, and from it flowed living waters, and the waters were called the jordan of truth. Every soul that is born comes down by that river, and every soul that is perfected goes up by it, and the river does not diminish, and it does not grow.
[Ginza Rabba, Right III — The soul's descent]

The soul came down from the House of Life into the body as into a garment, and the body said: Stay with me, and the world said: Stay with me, and the soul wept, for it remembered the House it came from, and its weeping was its prayer.
2: A call went forth from the House of Life: Who will go down to the prisoners and open their eyes? And Hibil Ziwa, the beloved, said: I will go down, and I will bring them up, and I will not forget one. And he went down, and the gates were opened, and the darkness hated him, and he was not moved.

Whoever goes down into the living water goes down into truth, and whoever rises from it rises into witness. Put on the white garment of the soul, and let no stain be upon it, for the garment is your word, and your word is your garment, and both are seen together.
[Ginza Rabba, Right XII — The double witness]

Blessed is he who has been baptized in truth and has kept his baptism clean. Blessed is the mouth that speaks no lie and the hand that takes no bribe, for such hands can lift a soul, and such a mouth can name the Name.
3: [Ginza Rabba, Left I — The soul's ascent]

When the soul leaves the body it goes up through the watch-houses, and at each gate it is asked: What did you do on earth? And the soul answers not with its works but with its truth, and the truth is the password, and the password is the Name, and the Name opens every gate.

The scales of the Life are true scales: a handful of mercy outweighs a mountain of show, and a cup of water given in the Name outweighs a river of gold. Weigh your deeds daily, and the scales of the last day will not surprise you.

And the Great Life promised the souls: You came down weeping, and you shall go up rejoicing. The body is a loan, and the world is a passing inn, but the House of Life is yours from of old, and its door is open, and the table is set, and your name is written upon your seat.
